battle.name: 紅巾軍抗金起義
battle.brief: 建炎元年春，汴京陷落，二帝北遷，兩河民眾以紅巾裹頭，聚眾抗金。九月，澤州、潞州的忠義民兵夜襲金朝左副元帥完顏宗翰的大寨，宗翰幾乎被擒。金軍屢次出師搜捕皆無所獲。一一二七年的攻城仍靠人力挽索的砲石車，配重投石車要等蒙古軍東來才到中土。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 交戰的兩方，是金朝在河東的駐軍與以紅巾為號的兩河忠義民兵。金朝一方由左副元帥完顏宗翰統率西路軍：他本名粘沒喝，漢語稱粘罕，小名鳥家奴，是金國相完顏撒改的長子，自金太祖、金太宗到金熙宗三朝都是宿將，天會三年（一二二五年）自大同向西攻宋，攻破太原，最終參與攻陷汴京。他麾下除女真本部兵外，還有編入金帳的漢人隊伍，其中一部就是金人收編的原遼朝義勝軍——金人一度收得遼籍漢人民兵十餘萬，讓他們守城、護路、押運糧秣。民兵一方沒有建制，也沒有統一指揮系統；他們是河東、河北兩路民眾在金軍佔領之下自發組織的忠義武裝，臨時以紅巾裹頭為號，便於散兵集結與彼此辨認。金朝不承認這支武裝的地位，視之為盜匪，屢次出動大軍搜捕。金朝在佔領區另扶植張邦昌的大楚傀儡政權，建炎元年三月初七日即位，四月金軍北撤時即被廢。與此同時，康王趙構於建炎元年五月初一在南京應天府即位，改元建炎，中原遺民多以此為恢復之望，但民兵義軍始終不受付南宋朝廷節制。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Jin garrison in the Hedong circuit and the loyalist militias of the two rivers that took the red headscarf as their badge. On the Jin side, the force in the field was the western army commanded by the Left Vice-Commander-in-Chief Wanyan Zonghan: his original personal name was Niamohe, he was known in Chinese speech as Nihan, and his childhood name was Niaojiunu. He was the eldest son of the Jin chancellor Wanyan Sagai and a veteran who served under Jin Taizu, Jin Taizong and Jin Xizong in turn. In the third year of Tianhui, that is 1125, he drove westward from Datong against Song, broke the city of Taiyuan, and ultimately took part in the fall of Bianjing. Besides the Jurchen troops of his own banner he had Han Chinese units incorporated into the Jin camp, among them men of the former Liao loyalist army, the Yishengjun: the Jin had enrolled more than a hundred thousand such Han Chinese from Liao, and set them to holding cities, escorting roads and moving grain. The militia side had no formation and no unified command structure. They were loyalist armed bands that rose spontaneously among the people of the Hedong and Hebei circuits under Jin occupation, and who tied a red cloth around the head as a temporary badge, so that scattered men could find one another and rally at a moment's notice. The Jin court never recognised this force as legitimate; it treated it as banditry and repeatedly dispatched field armies to hunt it down. In the occupied districts the Jin also propped up the puppet regime of the Great Chu state under Zhang Bangchang, who was enthroned on the seventh day of the third month of Jianyan and discarded when the Jin army withdrew north in the fourth month. At the same time the Prince of Kang, Zhao Gou, proclaimed himself emperor at Nanjing Yingtian on the first day of the fifth month of Jianyan and changed the era to Jianyan, and the surviving people of the Central Plains took hope from that. The militias, however, were never under the command of the new Southern Song court.
people: 完顏宗翰是本役最關鍵的敵方人物，也是最險的目標。他是金國開國功臣之後，天會三年主張攻宋，統西路軍自大同南下，攻太原、破真定，靖康元年與東路軍完顏宗望會師兵臨汴京，靖康二年參與城破之役，俘宋徽宗、宋欽宗北去。宗翰下令二帝脫去龍袍、廢為庶人，抗金名臣李若水在旁大罵不止，被割舌、挖目、斷手而死，至死方絕聲。東路主帥完顏宗望主持了第一次汴京圍城與宣和和議，擄康王趙構與宰相張邦昌為質，其後再圍汴京，才是宗翰與宗望兩軍合圍。金太宗完顏晟在遠方以天會五年年號發號施令，下詔廢二帝、准立張邦昌、驅二帝北遷，是這一串事件的最高決策者。另一方的人物多在事後才顯出分量：張邦昌以傀儡身分登基又覆亡；趙構在建炎元年五月朔於南京應天府即位；宗澤同年六月至建炎二年春知開封府，收復兩河之志不衰，曾自請以身作帥渡河；王倫奉命出使雲中被宗翰扣留，宗翰還把俘獲的宗室女眷賞給他。義軍方面，現存記載並未留下統一的首領姓名，這是本役史料最薄弱的一環；義軍多以鄉里、宗族為單位聚合，首領往往出自地方豪族、舊軍人與寺院道觀的組織者，各自為戰，行動互不統屬。
peopleEn: The decisive figure on the opposing side was Wanyan Zonghan, and he was also the person in greatest danger. A descendant of the founding merit of the Jin state, he had urged the campaign against Song in the third year of Tianhui, led the western army south from Datong, took Taiyuan and broke Zhending, and in 1126 joined the eastern army of Wanyan Zongwang before the walls of Bianjing; in 1127 he took part in the assault that ended the city and in the removal north of the Song emperors Huizong and Qinzong. It was Zonghan who ordered the two emperors stripped of their dragon robes and reduced to common status, and when the anti-Jin minister Li Ruoshui shouted abuse at the side of the captives, Zonghan had his tongue cut out, his eyes gouged and his hands severed, and Li did not fall silent until the end. The eastern commander Wanyan Zongwang had conducted the first siege of Bianjing and the Xuanhe peace settlement, taking the Prince of Kang Zhao Gou and the chancellor Zhang Bangchang as hostages; it was only afterwards that the two armies of Zongwang and Zonghan closed around the city together. Jin Taizong Wanyan Sheng, far away, issued the orders in the fifth year of Tianhui, decreeing the two emperors abolished, approving the enthronement of Zhang Bangchang and sending the captives north, and was the highest decision maker in the whole chain of events. On the other side, several figures only came into their own afterwards: Zhang Bangchang rose and fell as a puppet; Zhao Gou was enthroned on the first day of the fifth month of Jianyan at Nanjing Yingtian; Zekai governed Kaifeng as prefect from June 1127 into the spring of the following year, never weakening in his resolve to recover the two rivers, and once offered to lead the army across the river himself; and Wang Lun, sent on an embassy to Yunzhong, was detained by Zonghan, who even bestowed captured members of the imperial clan upon him. On the side of the militia, the surviving records leave no name for a single overall leader, which is the weakest link in the evidence for this campaign. The bands gathered by village and by clan, their leaders commonly drawn from local strongmen, former soldiers and men who organised things through temples and Taoist shrines; they fought each for themselves and their movements were not subordinated to one another.
kits: 卡面這件配重投石車並沒有出現在一一二七年的澤州與潞州戰場，也沒有出現在金軍攻陷汴京的攻城序列中。配重式投石機是十二世紀初在地中海世界出現的新器械，當時掌握在拜占庭、十字軍國家與義大利城邦的工匠手上，靠重臂末端的配重把石彈甩過城牆，所需操作人員不過數人，與中國的砲石車是兩種原理。它真正進入中土要等到十三世紀：蒙古軍把中亞與波斯的工匠帶入中原，這種機器以回回砲之名出現在宋金戰場，於襄陽攻守戰中大顯威力，砲聲先是震動全城守軍，繼而重創城樓，使守方無法再靠加厚牆身抵禦。一二二七年的中國攻城器械另有體系：北宋《武經總要》所載的砲石車屬橫臂人力挽索式，發射前要數十人以至百餘人拉索，靠人海把石彈拋出，收放全靠人力，射程與精度都受牽制；金軍攻汴京時同時備有雲梯、攻城塔、壕車、撞竿、火箭與霹靂砲，攻城塔以溼牛皮蒙覆以防火，壕車則逼近城牆供人搭橋，宋軍守城以檑木、沸水、弓弩與石砲應之，靖康元年第一次圍城時宋軍曾以霹靂砲反擊，事後仍有一名操作砲手被朝廷梟首。民兵一方沒有攻城器械，紅巾只是識別用的裹頭布，手中是刀、矛、弓箭與農具改造的叉鎗，另有少量繳獲自金軍的殘件；他們的裝備完全服從流動作戰的需要，因此配重投石車這種需要固定基座與專人操作的攻城機器，對他們毫無意義，反而是金軍自帶的砲石車與壕車在守城與清剿中發揮作用。
kitsEn: The counterweight trebuchet on the card was not present on the battlefield at Zezhou and Luzhou in 1127, nor in the siege train with which the Jin army took Bianjing. The counterweight throwing engine was a new machine that appeared in the Mediterranean world in the early twelfth century, held at the time by the engineers of Byzantium, of the crusader states and of the Italian city republics: it hurled a stone over a wall by means of a heavy counterweight at the end of the long throwing arm, and needed only a handful of men to work it, which is a different principle altogether from the stone-throwing engine of China. The machine did not truly reach the Chinese mainland until the thirteenth century, when Mongol armies brought craftsmen from Central Asia and Persia with them; it then appeared on Song and Jin battlefields under the name of the Huihui pao, the counterweight trebuchet, and made its name in the siege of Xiangyang, where the report of the stones shook the defending garrison throughout the city and then brought down a tower, leaving the defenders unable to rely on thickened walls alone. Chinese siege machinery in 1127 belonged to a different system. The stone-throwing engine recorded in the Northern Song military manual Wujing Zongyao is of the horizontal-arm, human-traction type: dozens and in some cases more than a hundred men haul on ropes to throw a stone, the machine is worked entirely by muscle, and both range and accuracy are constrained by that. When the Jin army attacked Bianjing it also had scaling ladders, siege towers, gangways, battering rams, fire arrows and thunder-crash bombs; the siege towers were sheathed in wet oxhide against fire, and the gangways were run up against the wall to give the assaulting men a bridge. The Song defended with logs, boiling water, crossbows and stone missiles, and during the first siege of Bianjing in 1126 the Song answered with thunder-crash bombs, after which one of the men serving the bomb was still executed by the court. The militia had no siege equipment at all: the red cloth was nothing but a badge tied round the head, and in their hands were knives, spears, bows and farm implements turned into prongs, with a few pieces taken from captured Jin kit. Their equipment was entirely governed by the needs of mobile warfare, and a machine like the counterweight trebuchet, which needed a fixed base and trained crews, meant nothing to them; it was the Jin army's own stone-throwing engines and gangways that did the work of holding cities and of clearing the countryside.
tactics: 民兵的打法完全建立在流動性上。史載紅巾軍戰時集中、散時隱蔽於民間，一旦金軍出動便四散歸村，金軍每次出師都無所獲；他們也沒有把屯營設在固定村落，而是以紅巾為暗號分散集合、夜間襲擊金軍的營寨、哨所與糧道，目標是營務而非城池。澤州與潞州之間約八十公里，距汴京不足二百公里，太行山南麓的山道與汾河谷地的村堡給了他們夜間移動的條件，這是金軍以騎兵與重步兵為主的追擊線所難以覆蓋的。金軍的應對則是把主力分屯各州縣城鎮，以軍官率部搜捕鄉里、斷絕接濟，逼民兵無法取得糧秣與鐵器補充；宗翰本人屢次聽聞各營寨被襲，遂令出兵捕拿，但每次皆空。其結果是金軍以重兵換不到殲滅，士氣與駐防疲於奔命。攻城一方的技術則在另一條線上：靖康元年第一次圍汴京時，尚書右丞李綱用百步法分兵，四壁每壁用正規軍一萬二千人，馬步軍編為前、後、左、右、中四軍各八千人分置將官，四日之內整備城防，金軍夜攻宣澤門、通天門與景陽門均被頂回，宋軍還以敢死隊出城夜襲；第二次圍城時宋將郭藥師為內應，開封門一度被開，金軍得以入城，說明守城一旦內應失效，牆體與器械再多也撐不住。配重投石車在這套邏輯裡毫無位置：它能一擊摧毀一段城牆，卻需要固定的基座、穩定的配重與專人操作，既無法隨軍移動，也不能對付四散在村落中的民兵。
tacticsEn: The way the militia fought rested entirely on mobility. The records state that the red-scarf troops concentrated for battle and hid among the populace when dispersed, breaking up into villages as soon as the Jin moved out, so that every Jin sortie came back empty. They did not fix their camps in permanent settlements either; using the red cloth as a signal, they gathered in dispersed groups and struck at the Jin encampments, outposts and supply lines by night, aiming at the camp service rather than at cities. Zezhou and Luzhou lie about eighty kilometres apart and less than two hundred kilometres from Bianjing, and the tracks along the southern foot of the Taihang Mountains and the villages and stockades of the Fen River valley gave them the conditions for moving at night, along routes hard for a Jin pursuit force of cavalry and heavy infantry to cover. The Jin answer was to distribute the main body among the walled seats of the prefectures and counties, sending officers with detachments to sweep the countryside and cut the militia off from supplies, so that they could obtain neither grain nor iron. Zonghan himself, hearing again and again that camps were being raided, ordered troops out to take them, and each time found nothing. The result was that the Jin spent great numbers of men and gained no destruction, while the morale and the garrison duty of the troops suffered from endless marching. The techniques of the besiegers ran on a different line. During the first siege of Bianjing in 1126 the Right Vice Minister of the Board of Works, Li Gang, apportioned the troops by the hundred-pace system: each of the four walls was held by twelve thousand regular soldiers, and the cavalry and infantry were organised into five armies of eight thousand men each, front, rear, left, right and centre, placed under separate officers, with the defences of the city readied within four days. The night attacks on Xuanze Gate, Tongtian Gate and Jingyang Gate were all thrown back, and the Song sent suicide squads out of the city by night in return. When the city was besieged a second time, the Song general Guo Yaoshi acted as an insider and the gate at Kaifeng was opened, which allowed the Jin in; the lesson is that once an insider fails, no amount of wall and equipment will hold the city. The counterweight trebuchet has no place in that reasoning. It can destroy a section of wall in a single blow, but it needs a fixed base, a steady counterweight and trained crews: it cannot travel with an army, and it cannot answer a militia scattered among villages.
data: 關於本役的數字，可信者不多，須分別看待。靖康元年第一次汴京圍城，李綱自述勤王之師集於城下者二十餘萬，金兵十萬，東京城被圍凡三十三日；第二次圍城時，金軍兵馬約十五萬，宋方守軍與勤王兵約七萬，圍城約一月，終至城破。時間線清楚：靖康二年正月初宋欽宗再赴金營被扣，二月初六金太宗下詔廢徽、欽二帝為庶人，三月初七金人立張邦昌為大楚皇帝，三月二十七與四月初一金軍退師、二帝北遷，同年五月初一趙構在應天府即位。紅巾軍的關鍵一役在建炎元年九月，澤州、潞州兩地民兵夜襲完顏宗翰的大寨，宗翰幾乎被俘殺；其後金軍多次出擊搜捕皆無所獲。里程上，澤州治晉城至潞州治長治約八十公里，至汴京不足二百公里。器械方面，《武經總要》所載砲石車每次發射需百餘人挽索，石彈重數十斤，一日之內能投的次數有限；反觀配重投石車只須數人操作、單次石彈可達數十至百餘斤，效率高出一個量級——但這是十三世紀之後進入中國的機器，與本役無關。金將完顏宗翰生於一〇八〇年，卒於一一三七年，帥齡五十八歲。
dataEn: Few figures survive for this campaign and they have to be weighed separately. During the first siege of Bianjing in 1126, Li Gang put the number of loyalist troops massed beneath the city at more than two hundred thousand against a Jin force of one hundred thousand, and the city stood besieged for thirty-three days. At the second siege the Jin had about one hundred and fifty thousand men and the Song, counting garrison and relief troops, about seventy thousand; after roughly a month the city fell. The chronology is firm: in the first month of 1127 the Song emperor Qinzong went again to the Jin camp and was detained; on the sixth day of the second month Jin Taizong decreed the two emperors reduced to commoners; on the seventh day of the third month the Jin set up Zhang Bangchang as emperor of Great Chu; on the twenty-seventh day of the third month and the first day of the fourth the Jin army withdrew and the captives were taken north; and on the first day of the fifth month of the same year Zhao Gou was enthroned at Yingtian. The decisive action of the red-scarf troops came in the ninth month of Jianyan, when the militias of Zezhou and Luzhou attacked Wanyan Zonghan's main camp by night and very nearly took him prisoner; afterwards repeated Jin sorties failed to find them. As to distances, the seat of Zezhou at Jincheng stands about eighty kilometres from the seat of Luzhou at Changzhi and less than two hundred kilometres from Bianjing. On the equipment side, the stone-throwing engine recorded in the Wujing Zongyao needed more than a hundred men on the ropes for each throw and sent a stone of several tens of jin, so that the number of shots possible in a day was limited; the counterweight trebuchet by contrast needed only a few men and could throw a stone of several tens to more than a hundred jin, an order of magnitude more efficient, though that was a machine that only entered China after the thirteenth century and has nothing to do with this campaign. The Jin general Wanyan Zonghan was born in 1080 and died in 1137, so he was fifty-eight years old.
cause: 起義的根由，是金軍在兩河地區的佔領與搜刮。宣和七年（一二二五年）八月，金太宗以張覺事變為由下詔攻宋，分東、西兩路南下：東路完顏宗望自平州破燕山府，中山、真定接連淪陷；西路完顏宗翰自大同攻太原，久攻不下而牽制全局。靖康元年正月二十六日，東路軍渡河抵汴京城下，李綱守城，金軍逼和，割中山、河間、太原三鎮，並索康王趙構與宰相張邦昌為質，勒出金銀數百萬，是為宣和和議。同年秋，西路軍攻破太原；閏十一月兩路合圍汴京，一月而城破，宋徽宗、宋欽宗被俘北遷。這場戰役之後，金軍分兵據守河東、河北各州縣，強徵糧秣、徵用民夫，把兩河當作持續抽取的兵源與糧源；忠義民兵於是紛起，以鄉里為單位打擊金軍的營寨與糧道。紅巾成為他們的標記，一半是為了在群眾與官軍之間自別，一半是為了讓分散的人手一望即知可以集合。金朝對此的定性很清楚——不是叛軍，而是盜匪，因此不談招撫，只談搜捕，這也決定了這場起義自始就不可能取得任何合法的政治地位。
causeEn: The root of the rising was the Jin occupation and extraction in the two river circuits. In the eighth month of 1125 Jin Taizong, on the pretext of the Zhang Jue incident, ordered the attack on Song and sent two armies south, an eastern and a western. The eastern army under Wanyan Zongwang broke through Pingzhou to Yanyan and took Zhongshan and Zhending in turn; the western army under Wanyan Zonghan came down from Datong against Taiyuan and was held there, delaying the general plan. On the twenty-sixth day of the first month of 1126 the eastern army crossed the river to the walls of Bianjing, where Li Gang held the city, and the Jin forced a settlement: the three circuits of Zhongshan, Hejian and Taiyuan were ceded, the Prince of Kang Zhao Gou and the chancellor Zhang Bangchang were taken as hostages, and several hundred thousand in gold and silver were squeezed out, in what is called the Xuanhe peace settlement. In the autumn of the same year the western army broke Taiyuan, and in the intercalary eleventh month the two armies closed around Bianjing and took the city within a month, carrying Song Huizong and Song Qinzong north as captives. After that the Jin divided their troops to hold the prefectures and counties of Hedong and Hebei, compelling grain and levying labour, treating the two rivers as a standing source of soldiers and supplies to be drained. Loyalist militias accordingly rose in many places, striking at the Jin camps and supply lines village by village. The red cloth became their badge, half to distinguish them from the population and from the official troops, and half so that scattered men would know at a glance when to assemble. The Jin court's judgement on this was unambiguous: this was not rebellion but banditry. There was no talk of amnesty, only of capture, and that is what decided from the outset that this rising could never win any legitimate political position.
impact: 紅巾軍沒有改變北宋覆亡的結果——他們起義時汴京早已陷落，二帝已在北遷途中——但這支武裝在河東留下的影響卻超出戰役本身。金軍為剿滅義軍而屢次出師、往來於澤潞之間，兵馬與糧秣在無休止的搜索中消耗，客觀上分散了它南下與西進的力量，也讓南宋初年處於極度困難的局面下，多了河東一線騷擾與牽制的力量。名號的傳承則是一條容易誤導人的線：一二二七年河東民兵以紅巾為號，是為了戰時辨認彼此；一百二十餘年後，至正十一年（一三五一年）韓山童、劉福通在河南潁上舉事，同樣樹紅旗、裹紅巾，寫入史書的紅巾軍指的是那一批人，與澤州、潞州的民兵並無組織上的承襲關係，卻沿用了同一個符號。金朝在佔領區的統治方式也加深了矛盾：天會七年（一二二九年）金太宗下令禁民著漢服、髮式不得不如女真式，試圖以風俗與制度把佔領地改造為己有，結果只是把更多原本已願意合作的鄉里推向抵抗一邊。更深一層的影響在抗金傳統：兩河忠義武裝此後成為南宋初年北方抗金的重要一環，宗澤知開封府時便倚重義軍與民間武力的配合，收復兩河的呼聲也正是從這些義軍的實踐中來的。
impactEn: The red-scarf troops did not change the outcome of the fall of the Northern Song; by the time they rose, Bianjing had long been lost and the two emperors were already on the road north. Yet the effect this force had in Hedong went beyond the campaign itself. The Jin marched out again and again to hunt it down, shuttling between Zezhou and Luzhou, and horses, men and grain were consumed in endless searching; that objectively divided the Jin strength that might have gone south or west, and in the extremely difficult situation of the early Southern Song it added to the distant Chinese a line of harassment and pinning in Hedong. The transmission of the name itself is a thread easily misread. The red headscarf of 1127 was for telling comrades apart in battle; a hundred and twenty years later, in the eleventh year of Zhizheng, that is 1351, Han Shantong and Liu Futong rose at Yingshang in Henan, raised red banners and tied red scarves in exactly the same way, and the Red Turban Army written into the histories means that later band, which had no organisational descent from the Zezhou and Luzhou militia even though it borrowed the same sign. The way the Jin governed the occupied districts deepened the friction as well: in the seventh year of Tianhui, 1129, Jin Taizong forbade the people to wear Han dress and ordered hair to be cut not otherwise than the Jurchet fashion, trying to remake the occupied land as his own by custom and by institution, and in the result only pushed more of the villages that had been willing to cooperate into open resistance. The deeper influence lay in the tradition of resistance to the Jin. Loyalist armed bands of the two rivers became afterwards an important part of the northern anti-Jin effort of the early Southern Song; when Zekai was prefect of Kaifeng he relied on the combination of such militias and local fighting strength, and the call to recover the two rivers drew its force precisely out of the practice of these bands.
result: 結果是一場沒有勝負的消耗戰。建炎元年九月，澤州、潞州的民兵確實攻入金軍大寨近處，完顏宗翰幾乎被當場擒殺，這是全役最接近成功的一擊；但義軍沒有攻城器械、沒有糧秣積存、沒有一個能持續指揮的總部，攻擊過後無法佔據營壘，也無法把成果轉成據點。金軍轉而以屯駐據點、搜捕鄉里、斷絕民間鐵器與糧秣供應來對付，把游擊戰拖成漫長的消耗，最後靠的是兵力與補給的總量，而不是戰術上的取勝。義軍的代價是組織潰散：一部分接受招安或被收編，併入南宋在北方的軍事部署，一部分散入山區成為長期游擊的小股勢力，也有不少在金軍與官軍的夾縫中消失。紅巾軍作為一場短促而尖銳的插曲就此收場，北宋仍然亡於靖康二年五月之前，南宋在應天府以建炎元年立國，北方兩河此後長期是金、宋拉鋸的地帶。它的意義因此不在戰果，而在示範：它證明在失去全部國防力量的地區，民間武裝仍然可以對正規大軍構成實質威脅，而這一點在此後的宋金戰爭中被不斷重演。
resultEn: The outcome was a war of attrition with no victor. In the ninth month of Jianyan the militias of Zezhou and Luzhou did break into the near perimeter of the Jin camp, and Wanyan Zonghan very nearly was taken and killed on the spot; that was the blow that came closest to success in the whole campaign. But the militia had no siege equipment, no store of grain, and no headquarters capable of giving continuous direction, and after the attack they could not hold the camp nor convert the blow into a base. The Jin turned instead to holding fixed posts, sweeping the countryside and cutting the people off from iron and grain, dragging what had been a guerrilla war into a long grind, and in the end it was won by the sheer weight of numbers and supply rather than by any tactical victory. The cost to the militia was the breaking up of its organisation: part of it was taken over or absorbed into the Song military deployment in the north, part scattered into the hills as small bands of long-term partisan warfare, and much of it simply disappeared in the gap between the Jin and the government troops. As a short and sharp episode, the Red Turban rising ended there. The Northern Song had still perished before the fifth month of 1127; the Southern Song founded itself at Yingtian under the era Jianyan; and the two rivers remained for long afterwards a contested ground between Jin and Song. Its significance therefore lay not in its results but in its demonstration: that in a region stripped of every regular defensive force, an armed populace could still pose a real threat to a professional army, and that lesson was repeated again and again in the Song-Jin war that followed.
